rationale: Six physical evidence channels distinguish malignant nuclei: log(worst radius), worst concave points, averaged mean/worst texture, worst smoothness, worst symmetry, and log(radius standard error / mean radius). Log transforms represent relative growth and heterogeneity and reduce right-skew; fixed logarithmic secants implement them with ReLUs. Each channel is centered at its two class means and divided by the pooled within-class standard deviation computed on a fixed 256-row construction partition. Explicit channel weights [1.8,1.6,0.9,0.75,0.4,1.05] discount strongly correlated size/indentation and smoothness/symmetry evidence while keeping texture and size-normalized variability independent. A one-dimensional Gaussian density ratio of the resulting scalar score provides an analytic slope and midpoint bias, plus smoothed class prior. No weight search or optimization. Local 85-row holdout is excluded from every supervised statistic. Missing indicators are unused because all support measurements are present.
